case.title: Cyber Terrorism Case Study Investigation
case.subtitle: Forensic simulation inspired by the 2015 Ukraine electric power grid cyberattack
case.classification_note: The historical incident is widely documented as a destructive state-sponsored cyberattack against critical infrastructure. The term 'cyber terrorism' is debated in academic and policy literature; this prototype uses the incident as a case-study simulation for critical-infrastructure cyber investigation.
case.safety_note: All logs, IP addresses, domains, hashes, usernames and timestamps used in the live simulation are synthetic. No malware, exploit code, credentials or destructive capability is included.

historical_context.sector: Electric power distribution / industrial control systems
historical_context.impact: Three electricity distribution companies experienced outages; U.S. government reporting states approximately 225,000 customers lost power for about 1–6 hours.
publicly_documented_elements: Spearphishing attachments were used for initial access into enterprise environments.
BlackEnergy was used in the campaign and was associated with credential collection and command-and-control activity.
Attackers obtained access to control environments and remotely operated HMI systems.
Breakers were opened through malicious control actions, disrupting electricity service.
KillDisk destructive activity was used to make infected systems inoperable and complicate recovery.
Telephone denial-of-service activity was reported during the disruption, impeding customer reporting and response.
historical_context.simulation_disclaimer: Event timestamps and all evidence artifacts below are reconstructed for training and demonstration. They are not original evidence from the victim organizations.

evidence.name: Suspicious spearphishing email
evidence.preview: From: energy-report@training-example.org | Attachment: Grid_Update_Q4.doc | SPF: fail | DMARC: fail
evidence.finding: An unsolicited Office attachment was delivered to an operations-related mailbox. Header anomalies and attachment context make it a high-priority acquisition target.

evidence.name: Office child-process execution
evidence.finding: An Office process launched a system binary in a pattern consistent with malicious document execution. No payload is included in this project.

evidence.name: Credential capture indicator
evidence.preview: Alert: suspicious credential-input capture behavior | host=WS-OPS-07 | user=operator.lab
evidence.finding: The event indicates attempted credential collection behavior, supporting the hypothesis that valid accounts were later used for remote access.

evidence.name: Abnormal VPN authentication
evidence.finding: A valid operator account authenticated from a previously unseen source. The address is from RFC 5737 documentation space and is not a real attacker address.

evidence.name: Remote administration session
evidence.finding: A remote support session was established toward an HMI workstation, providing a plausible bridge from enterprise access into the control environment.

evidence.name: Unauthorized breaker commands
evidence.preview: HMI-CTRL-03 -> BREAKER-12 OPEN | BREAKER-14 OPEN | operator-session=remote-support
evidence.finding: Control commands opened multiple breakers outside the normal dispatch workflow, directly correlating cyber activity with operational impact.

evidence.name: Call-center denial-of-service pattern
evidence.preview: Inbound call rate increased 18x baseline | queue saturation=100% | source identifiers=rotating
evidence.finding: The simulated PBX records show a flood pattern occurring during the outage window, consistent with attempts to impede customer and operator communications.

evidence.name: Destructive disk-wipe alert
evidence.preview: Host=SCADA-SRV-02 | alert=boot-structure corruption attempt | process=unknown | execution blocked in simulation
evidence.finding: A destructive action targeting boot structures would hinder recovery and evidence preservation. The prototype only records the event; no destructive action is performed.

events.title: Suspicious email delivered
events.message: A crafted Office attachment reaches an operations mailbox.

events.title: Abnormal child process detected
events.message: Endpoint telemetry records Office spawning a system execution utility.

events.title: Credential capture behavior
events.message: Host monitoring reports suspicious credential-input capture activity.

events.title: Operator VPN account used from new source
events.message: A valid grid-operations account establishes a session from an unseen documentation-range IP.

events.title: Remote session reaches HMI workstation
events.message: A remote support path is used from a jump host to a control workstation.

events.title: Breaker OPEN commands issued
events.message: Multiple breaker-open commands appear in the HMI audit trail outside the normal dispatch workflow.

events.title: Operational outage confirmed
events.message: Simulated telemetry shows loss of service across affected feeders after unauthorized control actions.

events.title: Customer call center saturated
events.message: Synthetic PBX metadata shows a denial-of-service pattern during the outage window.

events.title: Destructive cleanup activity detected
events.message: A server sensor records simulated disk-wipe behavior associated with recovery disruption.

events.title: Forensic containment and preservation
events.message: Investigators isolate affected systems, preserve volatile and log evidence, and begin chain-of-custody documentation.
